title: Childcare Salary: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to calculate your annual childcare salary from an hourly rate using the 38-hour week. Includes award rates, casual loading, super, and tax estimates.
salarySummary: For a full-time childcare employee on the Children's Services Award, the minimum hourly rate for a Level 1 Educator is $28.81, giving an annual gross of approximately $56,934 based on a 38-hour week and 52 weeks.

faqs.q: How is my annual childcare salary calculated from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week (usually 38 for full-time) and then by 52 weeks. For example, $28.81 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $56,934 per year. If you work part-time, use your agreed weekly hours instead of 38.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading for childcare workers?
faqs.a: Under the Children's Services Award, casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For a Level 1 Educator, that means $28.81 + 25% = $36.01 per hour. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) checkbox on our timesheet automatically adds this for you.

faqs.q: Does superannuation count as part of my childcare salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your base salary. Your employer contributes 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. It is not included in your take-home pay but is part of your total remuneration package. Use our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Conversion from Hourly to Annual Pay

If you work in early childhood education, knowing your **childcare salary** in annual terms helps you compare job offers, budget, and plan for tax and super. The standard method is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, the ordinary hours are 38 per week under the Children's Services Award. This article explains the formula, the difference between minimum wage and award rates, casual loading, and what super and tax mean for your take-home pay.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a full-time role, we use 38 hours. For part-time, use your contracted weekly hours. The fortnightly equivalent is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two – useful if you are paid fortnightly.

For example, a childcare educator on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026) working 38 hours a week would earn:
- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72
- Fortnightly: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44
- Annual: $1,004.72 × 52 = $52,245.44

But most childcare workers are covered by the Children's Services Award, which sets higher minimum rates.

### Childcare Salary Under the Children's Services Award

The Fair Work Ombudsman's Children's Services Award 2010 classifies employees from Level 1 (Introductory Educator) to Level 8 (Director). From the first full pay period on or after 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%. The current minimum hourly rates include:
- Level 1 – Introductory Educator: $28.81
- Level 2 – Educator: $29.69
- Level 3 – Qualified Educator 1: $32.47
- Level 4 – Experienced Educator: $34.65
- Level 5 – Advanced Educator: $36.57
- Level 6 – Room Leader: $38.25
- Level 7 – Assistant Director: $40.00
- Level 8 – Director: $46.12

These rates apply to full-time and part-time employees. A full-time Level 1 Educator working 38 hours would have an annual **childcare salary** of $28.81 × 38 × 52 = $56,934.08. That is about $4,689 more than the National Minimum Wage annual figure.

### Casual Loading for Childcare Workers

Casual employees under the award receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements. For a casual Level 1 Educator, the rate becomes $28.81 × 1.25 = $36.01 per hour. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how this affects your annual estimate. On our [timesheet](/) you can check a box to add the 25% loading automatically – never type a rate that already includes casual loading.

A casual childcare worker on $36.01 per hour working 38 hours a week would earn:
- Weekly: $36.01 × 38 = $1,368.38
- Fortnightly: $2,736.76
- Annual: $71,155.76

Remember, casual employees are only paid for hours worked and must receive a minimum of two hours per engagement.

### Superannuation Is Paid on Top

Your employer must contribute superannuation guarantee of 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund. This is paid on top of your hourly rate, not deducted from it. The maximum contribution base for 2026–27 is $270,830. For a full-time Level 1 Educator earning $56,934, the super contribution would be $56,934 × 12% = $6,832.08, making the total remuneration package $63,766.08. Use the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page to see how this affects your total compensation.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross **childcare salary** is not what you take home. The Australian Tax Office (ATO) applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). For a $56,934 annual salary, the estimated tax would be approximately $8,367 plus Medicare of $1,139, leaving about $47,428 take-home pay. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page provides a more detailed breakdown.

### Using the Timesheet and Pay Guides

To calculate your own **childcare salary**, start with your base hourly rate from your award classification. Enter it into [the timesheet](/) and select your hours per week. The tool will show your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay. For award-specific allowances and penalty rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. The [reference tables](/data) also list current minimum wages for all classifications.

### Key Points to Remember

- The standard conversion assumes 38 hours per week for full-time. Part-time workers should use their actual weekly hours.
- Award rates for childcare are higher than the National Minimum Wage. Always check your classification under the Children's Services Award.
- Casual loading adds 25% on top of the base rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading.
- Super is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and capped at the maximum contribution base.
- Tax and Medicare are deducted from your gross pay. Use the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) pages for comparisons.

By understanding these components, you can confidently evaluate job offers and plan your finances. Whether you are an educator, room leader, or director, knowing your annual **childcare salary** empowers you to make informed career decisions.
